title: The Dream Machine
creator: M. Mitchell Waldrop
take: Through the biography of J.C.R Licklider we learn about the creation of the internet as we know it today, and how his vision carried us through the decades of WWII to the 90s. Bit of a hard read if there isn't a Computer Science background

title: The Cold Start Problem
creator: Andrew Chen
take: Mr. Chen walks us through the do's and don't's of some of the biggest tech companies today and how they conquered their respective networks. Really interesting read and has lots of useful and practical points on how to scale up your own startup

title: A Game of Thrones
creator: George R. R. Martin
take: The one that started it all, and perhaps a bit slower than the rest of the series just due to the amount of world building and setup that is required initially.

title: A Clash of Kings
creator: George R. R. Martin
take: This book quickly picks up where the first left off in suspense and doesn't let up. You get to read about some of the most amazing battles in fantasy and is enjoyable from end to end.

title: A Storm of Swords
creator: George R. R. Martin
take: Would be a 9/10 but it's sadly when things start to take a dip for one of my favorite characters in the series :( still an amazing story nonetheless

title: A Feast for Crows
creator: George R. R. Martin
take: Took the longest out of all the books to get through on my first read, especially with so many of my favorite characters not getting a POV in the book (and left on cliff hangers) but on my second read, realized I really enjoyed it especially Jaime's POV in the Riverlands

title: A Dance with Dragons
creator: George R. R. Martin
take: The longest one out of the series, and also the one where the show and the book are at a point completely different (I prefer the book). It's gotten a lot slower compared to the previous books as The War of The Five Kings wraps up and we deal with the fallout but the build-up of what's to come (if we ever get it) is so exciting that I can hardly wait (going on 15 years now)

title: Tokyo Vice
creator: Jake Adelstein
take: Super interesting about the only American journalist to work at the Japanese equivalent of the New York Times and his dealings with investigating and uncovering a large Yakuza dealing with the FBI. As someone who's a big fan of Japanese culture his experience living in Japan as a gaijin (outsider or foreigner) brought my view back to reality of what Japanese society is really like

title: One Piece
creator: Eiichiro Oda
take: One of the greatest manga's and world building of all time nothing comes close (maybe A Song of Ice And Fire) unfortunately it is a bit too long to get into at this point except for the most committed but still one of the greatest stories of all time

title: Five Families
creator: Selwyn Raab
take: Great book to learn about the history of the American Mafia from it's inception until about the mid 2000s. Tells actual stories of actual mobsters and doesn't glamorize it the way Hollywood often does.

title: Hunter x Hunter
creator: Yoshihiro Togashi
take: Only started reading this after finishing up the anime, personally think there is far too much information to be put into a manga and due to the inconsistent release schedule can be months or years between chapters released which is the only reason it has a low score. The story itself is phenomenal

title: It All Starts When You Do
creator: Kier Gaines
take: Current read: A bit skeptical of self-help books but personally have found this one to be very helpful in uncovering how I view myself, and helping me reconcile and heal the negative aspects of self-image, highly recommend

title: The Sopranos
creator: HBO
take: A show I quite literally watch over and over again on repeat, it's funny, has great drama and acting, the best quotes and has kind of spawned it's own internet subculture. Can sometimes be a little slow for some people to start

title: Boardwalk Empire
creator: HBO
take: A Peaky Blinders equivalent in America during Prohibition. Follows Nucky Thompson, Al Capone, Lucky Luciano, Arnold Rothstein etc. Really enjoyed how it showed so many historic crime figures of the era interacting and intersecting with each other. Found the ending to be a little lackluster imo. I also tended to like other characters over Nucky who's the main character like Lucky, Richard Harrow, Jimmy and Al Capone. Absolutely hated Margaret (practically all her scenes are skippable)

title: Peaky Blinders
creator: BBC
take: First season starts off a little slow but it's hard to not love Tommy or the rest of the gang, such an interesting story (did dislike the Luca Changretta season bc I found it to be such a fake unrealistic version of what the mob was actually like) otherwise amazing show, great acting, great characters, great story.

title: Top Boy
creator: Netflix
take: Never watched the original but really enjoyed this story about what it's like truly selling on the road. Not a 10 bc of what they did to my boy Jamie, also felt like the show struggled after he left

title: Snowfall
creator: FX
take: Franklin Saint what a character. Watching his rise and fall during the 80s crack epidemic is amazing. I disliked the later seasons truth be told but still the show is so bingeable. Made me a fan of Damson Idris and his acting especially all the scenes you see on TikTok all the time. Criminally underrated

title: Game of Thrones
creator: HBO
take: For the first 5 or 6 seasons this show is peak the closest thing to One Piece shot in the real world, but the fall off is something else once the show outpaced the books, hated the ending. Doubly hated once I read the books after and realized how badly they screwed up

title: The Blacklist
creator: NBC
take: First couple seasons are so fun but the show quickly gets repetitive. James Spader carries

title: Suits
creator: USA Network
take: Fun show but quickly gets repetitive, also found out from my lawyer friends that being a lawyer isn't as cool Harvey makes it out to be. Louis Litt is the goat

title: Stranger Things
creator: Netflix
take: The first couple seasons were so good but the timing between seasons made it hard to follow along and the ending was meh to say the least

title: Narcos
creator: Netflix
take: A half-documentary half-drama following the Medellin and Cali Cartels, found out it isn't too accurate but still really fun and you can pick up a bit

title: Money Heist
creator: Netflix
take: Super fun watch especially the first couple seasons but it quickly gets too big for it's own world (they have to keep pulling off crazier and crazier heists but that only works for how long?)

title: Lucifer
creator: Fox
take: Fun show but a little repetitive and probably a little haram to watch a show where the protagonist is literally Satan

title: All American
creator: The CW
take: First season or two were amazing but once they graduated college and the NFL and all that was too much (why can't it just be a show about an amazing wide receiver, why does he literally have to be the main character of the whole world) trying to make Spencer Him just makes it cringey

title: Naruto
creator: TV Tokyo
take: I loved the original Naruto and most of Shippuden until it betrayed itself in the end. It was about how anyone can accomplish their dreams regardless of where they come from but quickly became about how OP the Uchiha are, and how Naruto is the reincarnation of Space Jesus' son, still so cool animation wise and fights

title: Ozark
creator: Netflix
take: I really liked Marty and the show initially but as it evolved it became quite boring I felt like, and the ending sucked. I really only finished it because I couldn't not finish it

title: Hunter x Hunter
creator: Nippon TV
take: Maybe the only world that could compete with One Piece and A Song of Ice And Fire in terms of worldbuilding sadly Togashi is forever sick, such a good show. Chimera Ant arc was just hard to watch because of all the details in it nen-wise

title: Vinland Saga
creator: NHK
take: Loved watching Thorfinn's progression as a character, first couple seasons were awesome.

title: Avatar: The Last Airbender
creator: Nickelodeon
take: Probably carried by nostalgia but such a good show from start to finish

title: Hey Arnold!
creator: Nickelodeon
take: Another nostalgia carry but such a good show to sit back and enjoy even in mid-20s

title: One Piece
creator: Fuji TV
take: The story is great the anime is mid, just because they stretch it out sooo long and it's tough to watch

title: House of the Dragon
creator: HBO
take: Being generous bc it's A Song of Ice and Fire but this show isn't as good as the original, still a fun watch though too much time between seasons tho

title: Tokyo Vice
creator: HBO Max
take: Follows the book but I watched this first. Really good show I liked the ending more in the show than real life LOL

title: Criminal Minds
creator: CBS
take: Perfect to show to just sit back and watch

title: South Park
creator: Comedy Central
take: Hilarious show nothing else to say

title: Family Guy
creator: Fox
take: First few seasons are amazing but the show gets worse as it ages, last couple seasons are unwatchable

title: The Hundred Years' War on Palestine
creator: Rashid Khalidi
take: Maybe it's because I consider myself a history buff but I feel like I didn't learn much coming out of this book, and felt it the same story repeated multiple times over decades (I will say for someone who has no knowledge on the history there's much to learn from this). I did enjoy the chapters where he talked about his living in Beirut during the Lebanese Civil War because those were interesting times.

title: Prison Break
creator: Fox
take: First two maybe 3 seasons are amazing but again the scope of the show keeps getting bigger and bigger to the point where it feels a little unrealistic

title: Friends
creator: NBC
take: Current watch: Never was into sitcoms but really enjoying this for the first time despite being insanely late
